chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a dog touching something from the body of a man. He said: “He washes the place that it touched.”

key_terms.أَصَابَهُ: it touched him/it reached him; indicating the point of contact requiring purification
key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: the dog; the source of ritual impurity discussed in this ruling
key_terms.الْمَكَانَ: the place; the specific area that must be washed
key_terms.جَسَدِ: body; the human body part affected by contact
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes; the required act of purification

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a dog touches part of a person’s body according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning najasah from a dog contacting a person’s body. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that the specific area touched is to be washed, indicating the requirement of purification of the affected spot.
